title.narrative: WTO Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF)

description.narrative: The Standards and Trade Development Facility, a global partnership of the Food and Agriculture Organization, the World Organisation for Animal Health, the World Bank, the World Health Organization and the World Trade Organization, builds the capacity of developing countries to implement international sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) standards to gain and maintain international agricultural market access.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

title.narrative: External Evaluation of the Standards and Trade Development Facility

description.narrative: In nine Indo-Pacific countries (Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Vietnam), a project funded by the WTO Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) and led by the Asia-Pacific Association of Agricultural Research Institutions piloted an innovative approach to reduce pesticide residue levels affecting trade. Australia’s longstanding partnership with the STDF contributed to the project, which determined that the use of biopesticides alongside conventional pesticides could reduce pesticide residue levels by 50 per cent. The project harmonised regional guidelines on the use and trade of biological control agents, developed the capacity of over 170 government officials to meet international WTO and Codex standards, and created networks for public-private knowledge exchange and collaboration in beneficiary countries

Peppercorn farmers in Cambodia, Lao PDR and Vietnam face challenges meeting international World Trade Organization Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Agreement obligations and international food safety standards due to concerns around microbial contaminants and pesticide residues. This affects their ability to access international markets. Australia’s partnership with the Standards and Trade Development Facility contributed to the successful conclusion of a project to help peppercorn farmers boost food safety and gain access to new markets. The project enhanced the farmers’ SPS capacity, built confidence in the region’s industry, unlocked markets, strengthened rural economies, and raised incomes. Through adoption of biocontrol methods, pesticide use was reduced, contributing to environmental sustainability objectives, and local incomes were improved due to increased yields and higher prices. Cambodian peppercorns gained access to the Chinese market for the first time and farmers experienced a 10% increase in yields and 30% increase in incomes. Vietnamese peppercorn exports met 100% of food safety controls for the EU market, and Lao PDR farmers improved productivity and yield with prices rising from US$1,870 to US$4,343 over the course of the project. The project also started a grassroots partnership among regional peppercorn farmers to encourage community responsibility, peer learning, and good practices.

The Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) has contributed to increased sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) capacity, especially, with regard to World Trade Organization SPS Agreement obligations, in 19 developing countries. STDF projects contributed to enhancements in national legislation, strategies, structures and processes related to food safety, and plant and animal health. For example, as a result of STDF activities, Papua New Guinea developed national guidelines to eliminate smoke taint in cocoa, India developed a comprehensive National Contaminant and Residual Control Programme, and Guinea ratified an updated plant health law and implemented 3 regulations in line with international standards.
